title: The Mobilisation Gap: Why Your Biggest Win of the Year Can Be Your Tightest Month of Cash
linkedin:
You just won the biggest contract of the year. Three weeks later, the bank balance is tighter than before you signed it.

That isn't a sign something went wrong. It's a timing problem, and it catches well-run, profitable businesses more often than struggling ones, because the businesses doing the winning are usually the ones growing fastest.

Every new contract carries a mobilisation period: the stretch between saying yes and the first payment actually landing. Staff get hired, stock gets ordered, equipment gets bought, sometimes a bond has to be posted, and none of that waits for a payment schedule.

The revenue moves at the pace of the contract terms instead. Milestone billing, 30 to 60 day terms, a probation period before full volume kicks in. The cash coming in lags well behind the cash already spent.

Here's the part most owners don't see coming until it happens: the bigger the win relative to current revenue, the bigger the gap. A client worth an extra ten percent is manageable. A client worth fifty or a hundred percent creates a cash commitment on a completely different scale, funded by a business that was never sized for it.

The fix isn't turning down good contracts. It's modelling the mobilisation period before signing, not three weeks into it, so the tight month is expected and funded rather than a surprise.

Honest question for the business owners here: have you ever landed your biggest contract of the year and then watched the bank balance get tighter, not looser, in the weeks after?

It happens more than people admit. A big new client doesn't arrive with its own cash attached. Staff, stock and equipment all get paid for straight away, while the client's own payment terms mean the money coming back takes weeks, sometimes months, to catch up.

The bigger the win, the bigger that gap. It's not a sign anything went wrong. It's just timing, and it's worth planning for before you say yes, not after the invoices start piling up.

A quick note for business owners across Brisbane, Queensland and the broader East Coast as spring trading picks up and the bigger contracts start landing.

Winning the biggest client or contract of the year feels like the turning point every owner is chasing, and it should be celebrated. But a few weeks later, a lot of businesses notice the bank balance has actually gotten tighter, not easier, and it isn't obvious why.

The reason is timing. A new contract carries what we call a mobilisation period, the gap between saying yes and the first payment actually arriving. Staff need to be hired, stock needs to be ordered, equipment needs to be bought, and all of that gets paid for straight away. The client's own payment terms, milestone billing or a probation period before full volume, mean the cash coming back lags well behind the cash already spent.

The bigger the win relative to the size of the business, the bigger that gap tends to be. It isn't a sign anything has gone wrong. It's a mechanical timing issue that catches growing, profitable businesses more often than struggling ones.

The fix is modelling that gap before accepting the work, not three weeks into delivering it, so the tight month is expected rather than a surprise.
